species: rat (primary astrocytes and microglia); human (HEK293T cell line)
readout_other: Trypan blue exclusion cell viability assay and light microscopy of cell morphology; needle-hydrophone acoustic pressure-field mapping was used to characterize the device (not a biological modulation readout)
direction_notes: This is a device-engineering and validation paper for a 3-D-printed film-based cell culture/sonication vessel; no active-ultrasound modulation experiment on cells was reported. Ultrasound was used only (a) for acoustic pressure-field characterization with a needle hydrophone in a water tank (no cells present), and (b) for a device biocompatibility check in which cells were placed in the sealed device and immersed in the water tank for 15 min with ultrasound output disabled ('sham-sonication'), to confirm the device itself does not reduce cell viability.

timing.protocol_description: For pressure-field mapping (hydrophone in a water tank, no cells present), both the 500 kHz (Sonic Concepts H-107) and 1 MHz (Olympus A392S) focused transducers were driven with a 20 mV peak-to-peak voltage, 10-cycle pulse length, and 10 Hz pulse repetition frequency. This characterization was not applied to living cells; the only procedure involving cells and the device ('sham-sonication') used no active ultrasound output at all.

source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: Two focused ultrasound transducers were calibrated, one with a 1 MHz center frequency (Olympus A392S) and one with a 500 kHz center frequency (Sonic Concepts H-107). The pulse shape and sequence were generated by a function generator (33500B Series, Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA, USA) and were driven through an amplifier (2100L Electronics and Innovation, Rochester, NY, USA). The pressure intensity was measured in each position and recorded by a 14-bit oscilloscope with 100 MHz sampling frequency (GaGe model Octave Express CompuScope, DynamicSignals, Lockport, IL, USA). The pressure field was compared to that of a control setup, in which the platform, including the device, was removed from the setup. The height of the platform (z-direction) was manually adjusted to accommodate for the different focal lengths of the two transducers, ensuring optimal alignment and accurate pressure field characterization. The mean absolute error (MAE) and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) were determined using the peak-negative of each time-traces to evaluate the pressure differences with and without the setup.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_repetition_fre: Fig. 2. Horizontal experimental setup for pressure field mapping. The horizontal configuration facilitated the set-up process when measuring the pressure field with a needle hydrophone compared to a vertical setup requiring a tall water tank. It also provided greater control over the needle hydrophone by having more visible space to navigate within, lowering the risk of it being damaged. The tank was filled with degassed water. For both focused transducers (500 kHz and 1 MHz) following parameters were used: 20 mV peak-to-peak voltage, 10 cycle pulselength, and 10 Hz pulse repetition frequency.

flags.reason: This paper is a device/instrumentation validation study. No experiment reported delivering active ultrasound to living cells for a modulation or functional outcome; the only 'sonication' applied to cells was a 15-min immersion with ultrasound output disabled ('sham-sonication') to test device biocompatibility. Acoustic pressure-field characterization (500 kHz Sonic Concepts H-107 and 1 MHz Olympus A392S transducers, 20 mV peak-to-peak drive, 10-cycle pulse length, 10 Hz PRF) was performed with a hydrophone in water, not on cells. Given no biological ultrasound exposure/modulation experiment is reported, the exposures array is left empty rather than invented.

Cell viability testing used three samples per group ('Each group has three samples') across multiple cell types (primary astrocytes/microglia, HEK293T) and conditions (well plate, film outside device, film inside device with sham-sonication); the paper does not give a single total sample count, so the per-group n=3 is reported and flagged.

The 'sham-sonication' viability check placed cells in the device/water tank for 15 min without describing whether a transducer was mounted but powered off, or simply omitted; classified as inactive_transducer as the closest match, since this mimicked the sonication setup without acoustic output.

Added only to satisfy the non-empty exposures requirement; this reflects acoustic/hydrophone device characterization (no cells present), not a biological ultrasound exposure. See the exposures flag above for why no true biological exposure is reported in this paper.

provenance.notes: Device/methods paper describing a 3-D-printed cell-culture sonication vessel; contains acoustic pressure-field characterization data (Table I: MAE/MAPE for two transducers and three film materials) but no biological ultrasound-modulation exposure experiment.
